key_insight: Odd (Hall) viscosity can emerge microscopically in active chiral films when shear reorients torque-exerting anchored particles, creating a transverse traction from flow alignment.
engineering_relevance: This provides a controllable route to design surfaces or suspensions with nonreciprocal, nondissipative transport useful for microfluidic and active-matter flow control.
method: Built a kinetic theory for the orientational dynamics of anchored elongated particles under shear.
Derived the stress response and odd-viscosity tensor from shear-induced polarization and transverse surface traction.
Solved the nonlinear theory numerically to probe strong-shear saturation beyond linear response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical derivation plus numerical solutions showing saturation of transverse traction at strong shear, validating the emergent odd-response mechanism.
watch_item: The theory is for thin anchored active chiral films and may not transfer directly to unanchored or strongly three-dimensional active flows without additional modeling.
paper_title: Emergent odd response in active chiral films
